 Major NJ REAL ID Changes Underway Ahead Of Holidays: How To Get Yours
 Major overhaul to REAL ID appointments come just before the Garden State enters its busy holiday travel season. 
 Jack Slocum , Patch Staff 
 Posted Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 10:23 am ET | Updated Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 3:13 pm ET Those who still haven't gotten their REAL ID just got a big break, just before the holiday travel season, no less. 
 Earlier this year, getting a REAL ID could be considered a real drag, with wait times reaching up to 73 days. Now, the average appointment wait time is just three days, according to the Sherrill Administration. 
 “Government should make people’s lives easier,” said Governor Mikie Sherrill. “New Jerseyans were waiting an average of 73 days for a REAL ID appointment, and that was unacceptable. We made operational improvements at the MVC, and now residents can get an appointment in just three days as they prepare for holiday travel.”

 Officials said the dramatic cut in wait times — by over 96 percent — was thanks to "smart operational reforms," not an increase in spending.

 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . Specifically, the administration allowed the NJ Motor Vehicle Commission to accept digital proof of residency, including bank statements, pay stubs, and other digital documents rather than physical paper ones. 
 Furthermore, the administration streamlined document verification and expanded REAL ID services to seven more NJMVC agencies this year, officials said. 
 “We solved capacity challenges by working smarter, not spending more,” said Acting NJMVC Chief Administrator Rosalie Johnson. “These targeted changes are proof government can deliver better results through creative thinking and improved operations.”
 Can I Fly Without A REAL ID? 
 The Sherrill Administration encouraged residents to get their REAL IDs sooner rather than later, with Thanksgiving just days away and further holiday travel adding to the Garden State's hustle and bustle. 
 Since May 2025, REAL ID-compliant driver licenses or identification cards have been required by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to board domestic flights. Standard New Jersey licenses and IDs without the REAL ID star symbol are no longer accepted at airport checkpoints, officials said. 
 Flyers without a REAL ID can use their passport or, using their standard license, pay a $45 fee for a TSA ConfirmID to attempt to verify their identity. However, TSA officials said there is no guarantee the identity will be verified. 
 How To Get A REAL ID 
 Those looking to get their REAL ID will need the following: 
 Two proofs of NJ residency: Residents will need to provide two proofs of residency, which can include a utility bill, bank statement, or mortgage/lease, to name a few. These items can be printed physically or presented digitally by smartphone or tablet. 
 Valid Social Security number (SSN): Residents must present a valid Social Security number when getting their REAL ID. If the NJMVC cannot verify a SSN, customers must provide proof which can include a Social Security card, W-2, or pay stub with full SSN.
 Proof of identity: Residents must show a primary document proving their identity, such as a passport or certified birth certificate, as well as secondary documents that add up to six REAL ID points. These documents must be paper, as digital proof of identity documents are not accepted. 
 The state has provided this checklist and this document selector tool to help residents navigate the REAL ID application requirements. 
 Residents can make appointments to get their REAL ID through the NJMVC's appointment portal . As of Tuesday morning, there were more than 124,000 appointments available, including some same-day availability. 
 Those who are due for a standard license renewal within the next three months can also upgrade their renewal to a REAL ID appointment, NJMVC officials said. 
 Residents should arrive at their appointments with all of the required paperwork and be prepared to pay $35 for a 4-year REAL ID, or $11 if they are upgrading ahead of their license renewal window and keeping its expiration date. 
 Once finished at the NJMVC, customers will get a temporary license and can expect their REAL ID in the mail within two weeks, officials said.
